newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ups import duties on eight U.S. products.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ups import duties on eight U.S. products.

text.p: The Mexican government said Thursday it was raising import duties on eight U.S. products in response to U.S. limitations on Mexican broom imports.
The import duties, published in the official government gazette, would affect fructose, wine, wine coolers, brandy, Tennessee whiskey, notebooks, float glass and some items of wooden furniture.

"This action is taken in full compliance with Mexico's rights under NAFTA, in response to the safeguard measure adopted adopted by the United States on imports of broom corn brooms from Mexico effective as of November 28, 1996," the trade ministry said in a statement.
Mexico said that it would continue to try and resolve the dispute under North American Free Trade Agreement mechanisms.

The U.S. action represented $1.02 million of additional taxes that the U.S. government could levy, the ministry said, so the Mexican response had "trade effects substantially equivalent to the safeguard adopted by the United States".
